claims.text: The modified alloy is equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is an FCC solid solution.
The proposed baseline is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co lowers the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co modifies local lattice distortion arising from atomic-size effects.
The Co-removal-induced changes in stacking-fault energy and local distortion facilitate dislocation cross-slip.
The Co-removal-induced changes facilitate deformation-twin nucleation at lower temperatures or lower strain rates than in the Co-containing alloy.
More readily activated cross-slip and twinning produce a smoother transition from work hardening to dynamic recovery.
The altered deformation mechanism reduces stress serrations.
Removing Co shifts the onset of ductile deformation to lower temperatures.
The altered mechanism enhances the dynamic strength-ductility balance of FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
At low temperatures, Co-free FeNiCrMn has lower yield strength than CoCrFeMnNi because dislocations are more mobile.
At a given strain rate, Co-free FeNiCrMn activates dynamic recovery and deformation twinning earlier than CoCrFeMnNi.
Under high-temperature, low-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn exhibits fewer or weaker stress serrations than CoCrFeMnNi.
Co-free FeNiCrMn gains ductility relative to CoCrFeMnNi without a severe loss of strength.
The proposed regime spans approximately 25 to 900 °C and strain rates of 1×10^-4 to 1×10^-3 s^-1.
The Co-free alloy remains an FCC solid solution without phase transformations throughout the proposed testing regime.
A matched comparison of Co-free FeNiCrMn and CoCrFeMnNi across temperature and strain rate can distinguish the proposed mechanism by measuring twinning, recovery, serrations, strength, and ductility.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Co-free alloy shows neither earlier nor significantly greater twinning and dynamic recovery, together with the predicted serration and ductility changes, relative to the baseline.
